newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Central Europe prepares joint drug crime fight.
newsitem.headline: Central Europe prepares joint drug crime fight.

text.p: Interior ministers and law enforcement officials of 12 central and east European countries agreed on Thursday to prepare a joint strategy to combat organised drug crime in the region.

The two-day conference of the Central European Initiative (CEI), also involving officials from Interpol and the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), focused on harmonising legislation to permit a joint effort in fighting drug crime.

Stanislav Becica, a senior Slovak Interior Ministry official, told a news conference that delegates agreed to recommend to a November meeting of CEI prime ministers that a working group should be set up to tackle the issue.
He said said the meeting discussed national anti-drug legislation which differed in many aspects such as punishment or the extent of tolerance of drug addicts.

The CEI group, originaly known as the Pentagonale, was set up in 1989 by Austria, Italy, Hungary, former Czechoslovakia and former Yugoslavia to develop stability, cooperation and integration in Central Europe.

"Drug abuse, with the significant increase of illegal drug trade in Central Europe mainly through so called Balkan route, has a general negative impact on the social-economic processes in the region," the ministers said in a joint statement.

Christopher Luckett, head of the anti-drug division for the Council of Europe, said central and east European countries needed to adopt clear classification and registration of drugs in order to come into line with U.N. conventions
"Then severe penalties for all types of drug trafficking, selling and joint activities must come," he added.
